stl_availability_probe.actual_include_test: #include <limits> inside RTC kernel compiles OK under default AND -nostdinc++ AND -nostdinc
interpretation: Linux wheel HIPRTC exposes full libc++ to device compilation by default -> unpatched MIOpen HIPRTC kernels that use <limits>/<utility> compile (matches historical Linux unpatched PASS; Windows lacks these paths, hence the Windows failure class)

-nostdinc and -nostdinc++ behave IDENTICALLY in this HIPRTC context: both remove <utility> only; <type_traits>/<limits>/<initializer_list> remain reachable via HIPRTC-internal include paths that -nostdinc does not suppress (plain clang++ -nostdinc++/-nostdinc outside HIPRTC removes all four - verified separately)

CONSEQUENCE: on Linux, neither flag is a complete STL isolation method; any validation requiring a Windows-like partial-STL environment must construct it differently (e.g., explicit header search path restriction). Recorded for the final A/B protocol.
